API index

API · trait

Codec

Messages · defined at codec.mbt:16

pub trait Codec {
  fn ty(Self) -> TypeId
  fn write_data(Self, Writer) -> Unit raise
  fn read_data(Reader, TypeId) -> Self raise
}

A value that knows how to become bytes, and how to come back from them.

The contract is one line: write_data and read_data are everything after the type ID. The type ID belongs to whoever knows the schema — a struct field to its FieldMeta, a list to its header, a map to its chunk header — and what follows belongs to the value, which is why a struct or an enum writes its user type ID here and not there.

Everything this package ships implements this trait, and a caller's own type implements it the same way: there is no second path for the types that come with the library.

Required methods

MethodMeaning
fn ty(Self) -> TypeId

The type ID: the number that begins a value of this type.

fn write_data(Self, Writer) -> Unit raise

Everything after the type ID.

fn read_data(Reader, TypeId) -> Self raise

Everything after the type ID, read back. ty is what the wire said, which is not always what the writer would have chosen: a peer's 1 may come as VARINT64, and an integer asked for as thirty-two bits may arrive as sixty-four.
